summary: Most travelers need a Syrian visa arranged before arrival: the UK, Canadian, German and Australian governments all tell their citizens to get one in advance, and Canada says non-Arab nationals cannot obtain one at Syrian border points. Gulf, Jordanian and Lebanese passports are shown as visa-free, but no official source we could read confirms the current rule for them; other Arab nationalities are shown as needing a visa through an embassy. Syria's embassy in Paris says visa applications must now be made online at evisa.sy, but the site was not yet taking applications on 3 October 2026 — ask a Syrian embassy how to apply shortly before travel.

tips.text: Entry rules are changing rapidly under the transitional government — reconfirm your visa, route and permits with a Syrian embassy and a reputable local operator days, not weeks, before travel.
Most governments still advise against all travel to Syria — if you go anyway, use an experienced local guide, share your itinerary with someone at home and register with your embassy where possible.
Travelers with Israeli stamps, visas or any other evidence of travel to Israel are refused entry. Use a clean passport.
Bring US dollars or euros in cash for the entire trip — foreign cards and ATMs do not work, and crisp, undamaged notes get the best rates.
Expect frequent checkpoints between cities. Carry your passport, visa and any permits at all times, and never photograph military or government sites.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Syria?
faq.answer: Almost certainly yes. Unless you hold a Gulf, Jordanian, Lebanese or Turkish passport, plan on getting a visa before you travel — that includes most other Arab nationalities. The UK, Canadian, German and Australian governments all say their citizens need one in advance, and Canada says non-Arab nationals cannot obtain one at Syrian border points. Syria's embassy in Paris says applications must now be made online at evisa.sy, but the site was not yet taking applications on 3 October 2026, so ask a Syrian embassy how to apply.

faq.question: Can I get a Syrian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Do not plan on it. Visas on arrival at Damascus airport were reported for some Western nationalities in 2025, but the UK, Canadian, German and Australian governments now all say their citizens must have a visa before travel, and Canada states that non-Arab nationals cannot get one at Syrian border points. Arrange the visa before booking; ask a Syrian embassy how to apply while evisa.sy is not yet open.

faq.question: Is Syria safe to visit?
faq.answer: No — most governments advise against all travel. Damascus, Aleppo and the coast are calmer than during the war years, and organized tours do run, but unexploded ordnance, sporadic fighting, terrorism and detention risks remain real, and consular support is minimal. Anyone going should use experienced local guides and follow conditions daily.

faq.question: What money should I use in Syria?
faq.answer: Cash only. Bring US dollars or euros for your whole stay — international cards and ATMs do not work for visitors — and exchange into Syrian pounds in small amounts as needed. Clean, recent-series banknotes are strongly preferred.

faq.question: Can I visit Syria if I have been to Israel?
faq.answer: Israeli citizens cannot enter Syria, and the UK government warns that travelers whose passport shows previous travel to Israel may be refused entry. Travel on a passport without such evidence.
